title: Week one as a maker: viral directories, an acquisition offer, and why PH launches lost value
summary: John recaps a week across 20+ projects. Directory sites (allgpts, osssoftware) pulled big traffic, PH launches are losing value versus tweets and HN/dev.to posts, and virality does not equal revenue. He also shares lifetime-deal pricing for indexgoogle.

principles.text: You can't predict what will take off. Ship many projects and let the market tell you.
principles.quote: This shows you never know what will work until you try.

principles.text: Going viral doesn't mean making money. Traffic without paying conversions is not product-market fit.
principles.quote: Going viral doesn't always mean making money - an unexpected learning.

principles.text: Product Hunt launches are worth less now than tweets or posts on Hacker News and dev.to.
principles.quote: I'm stepping back from promoting PH launches as they don't seem valuable anymore compared to tweets or posts on hackernews or devto.

principles.text: Directory sites can pull big traffic cheaply. Offer a directory template so users can build them too.
principles.quote: unicornplatform.com got a big push from our new "directory" template. Users quickly create cool directories at low cost.

principles.text: Signal an exit publicly to gauge price and demand. Then decide using the stats, and keep the asset if the upside is bigger.
Price some tools as a one-time lifetime fee instead of a subscription.
principles.quote: $99 per domain for life or $199 for five domains. No subscription, just a one-time fee.
